answer: One yarrow rack per identity, fed by one ember heater, locks an 80-credit bond keyed to a cipher seal serial. Per epoch it files stem count and fuel mass; the auditor recomputes moisture loss from the yarrow heat table and checks the cipher seal. Over 4 percent error, a reused serial, or a copied log burns the bond. The first filing costs 37 credits, the kth 37+6(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 6,031 and 1,000 fakes pay 3,034,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-rack ring fails because one heater cannot dry two racks; an honest keeper pays 37 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
